name: openbot
description: A local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. Run Codex, Claude, and Grok with dedicated workspaces, task queues, file sharing, browser control, and agent-to-agent collaboration.
one_liner: A desktop app that gives you a roster of AI 'teammates' (powered by whichever coding assistants you already have) that each keep their own files, task queue, and can message each other, running on your own computer.
buyer: A technical founder or small dev team lead who already pays for Claude/Codex/Grok and wants those tools to act like persistent coworkers instead of disconnected chat windows.
business_use_cases: A small dev team assigns one persistent agent per workstream (bug triage, docs, refactors) so work queues and context survive between sessions instead of resetting each chat.
A solo founder has agents hand tasks to each other (one researches, one drafts, one reviews) through the built-in agent-to-agent messaging instead of manually relaying context.
An agency runs a shared desktop channel so a human and multiple agents collaborate on one task with explicit delegation and hand-off controls.

money_ideas.idea: None baked in — it explicitly runs on the user's own agent subscriptions and local machine, so there's little to resell as a product.
Sell setup/configuration consulting for teams who want this but don't want to manage the self-hosted server piece themselves.

steal_this: It's explicitly in development preview with full-access agents and no per-action confirmation yet, which is a real safety flag — the honest weekend move is trying it solo on throwaway tasks, not pitching it to clients yet.
